newsitem.title: USA: Westpoint Stevens sells unit for $126 mln.
newsitem.headline: Westpoint Stevens sells unit for $126 mln.

text.p: WestPoint Stevens said Wednesday, that it has agreed to sell its Alamanac Knit Fabrics subsidiary to Dyersburg Corp for $126 million.
Almanac, which reported sales of $222 million in 1996 produces 100 percent cotton and cotton blend knit fabrics for sportswear and activewear makers, WestPoint said.

Under the terms of the transaction, Dyersburg will buy all of Almanac except its accounts recievable of approximately $42.5 million and a yarn mill located in Whitmore, S.C. That facility, the WestPoint said in a statement will be transfered to its Home Fashions business.

Halcombe Green, Jr., chairman and chief executive officer of WestPoint, commenting on the agreement, said, "The sale of our Almanac Knits subsidiary... is consistent with our corporate strategy to become a purely consumer products company focused on home fashions.
